rows.question: What does hands-on Databricks experience usually involve in these postings?
rows.answer:
Hands-on Databricks experience usually involves:

* Building solutions on Databricks in enterprise environments [1]
*  Hands-on Spark/PySpark expertise [2]

*  Converting Data Scientist notebooks into production pipelines with clear inputs, outputs, and fixed dependencies [3]
*  Setting up catalogs, schemas, storage credentials, external locations and volumes for landing zones and medallion layers across dev, test and prod [4]
*  Defining the grant model with account-level groups synced from Microsoft Entra ID; configuring service principals for jobs and CI/CD [4]
*  Working with Azure network teams on private endpoints for ADLS and Network Connectivity Configurations for serverless compute [4]
*  Implementing row-level or column-level security (RLS/CLS) in Databricks Unity Catalog [5]
*  Familiarity with Databricks Genie (AI/BI) or comparable self-service analytics tooling [5]
*  Experience with CI/CD for data pipelines (Databricks Asset Bundles, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or similar) [5]
*  Familiarity with Power BI or other BI tools consuming governed Gold-layer data [5]
*  Experience with API-based integration (REST/webhook patterns) and file-based integration (EDI, flat file, CSV) with validation controls [5]
